title: Observability hook amplification causing token-pipeline backpressure in Private clusters (hotfix)
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Multiple enterprise customers on Private clusters reported sustained first-token-time (TTFT) regressions and token/sec dropouts across model families after a recent observability rollout. Preliminary profiling points to synchronous observability hooks that amplify downstream RPC latency and cause microbatch handshake stalls in the token pipeline. This ticket coordinates the emergency mitigation, hotfix rollout, and postmortem action items.
impact_summary: Affected: Private/VPC clusters for 3 enterprise customers (finance, healthcare). Symptoms: TTFT increased by 200-700ms per request, tokens/sec dropped by 30-60% during high-fanout workloads. Severity: customer-facing SLA breaches and active escalations.
environments_affected: private (on-prem + VPC), limited observations on Dedicated when debug-tracing enabled; Hosted unaffected in default config
models_affected: observed across medium and large decoder-only models (open-8k, redwood-qa-13b-quant, customer-custom-13b variants) — effect amplified when streaming + tool-calls enabled
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy observability agent v2.7 with synchronous flush enabled to Private cluster
2) Run high-fanout prompt workload (50 concurrent sessions with streaming enabled) targeting open-8k model
3) Observe TTFT spike in Grafana trace (span waiting on observability flush) and multiplex handshakes stalling in node logs
4) Compare tokens/sec before/after rollout using /metrics/token_rate per worker
mitigation_actions: 1) Immediate rollback of observability agent v2.7 to v2.6 on affected clusters (performed at 2026-03-13T22:10Z) — removed synchronous flush path
2) Apply temporary token ingress throttle on private clusters to limit fanout to 60 sessions/unit (config change: infra/priv-config#fanout-limit)
3) Patch runtime to add async buffer for observability hook (PR linked below) and enable batching with 100ms flush window
4) Run canary on one customer cluster for 2 hours, validate TTFT and tokens/sec stability before global rollout

postmortem_action_items: 1) Change observability agent default to async-batched flush (timing: 100ms) and add feature-flag gating for private clusters
2) Add a runtime invariant that prevents synchronous external hooks from executing on the token emission critical path
3) Improve deploy gating: include simulated token-pipeline stress test in observability agent presubmit
4) Add dashboard alert for 'span_wait_time' > 50ms correlated with /metrics/token_rate drop > 20%
5) Document a customer communication template and escalate flow for observability-induced regressions
